stories.headline: Reliance to partner Rolls-Royce to develop fighter jet engines
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: In a boost to India's fifth gen fighter programme, 
Mukesh Ambani
's Reliance Industries Ltd and Rolls-Royce Friday announced they plan to jointly develop a sovereign indigenous combat engine for India's Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA).
As part of the partnership to design, develop, manufacture and deliver the same, Reliance and Rolls-Royce will explore formation of a dedicated aerospace gas turbine complex that will be a centre for power and propulsion technology in India.
The aero gas turbine complex will build sovereign, end-to-end Indian capability across design, development, manufacturing, testing, production and through-life support, while unlocking wider collaborations across defence, civil aerospace, and new power and propulsion systems.Aeronautical Development Agency under DRDO is officially designing and managing the AMCA project. As per initial planning, ADA is progressing with imported US GE F414 engines for the initial five AMCA prototypes under the Rs 15,000-crore programme. TNN

stories.headline: Pocso on online companies for child sex abuse content? SC to examine
stories.bodyText:
A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran issued notice to Union govt through MeitY and law ministry
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Friday agreed to examine a plea seeking prosecution of social media and online platforms under the stringent Pocso Act for showing child sexual abuse content and not reporting it to police, reports AmitAnand Choudhary. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran issued notice to the Union govt, through the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY) and the ministry of law and justice. It asked the petitioner NGO, 'Just Rights for Children Alliance (JRCA)', to implead intermediaries in the case to ensure compliance with the court's 2024 judgment.

stories.headline: Strong 7.7-magnitude quake strikes off Indonesia: USGS
stories.deck: Indonesia’s Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) warned of the possibility of tsunami waves being generated by the earthquake
stories.bodyText:
A strong 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck off Flores island in eastern Indonesia early on Saturday (August 15, 2026), the U.S. Geological Survey said.
The epicentre of the quake was located off the north coast of the island, about 68 km northwest of Ende, USGS said. The quake struck at a relatively shallow depth of just 10 km.
The initial quake was followed by two strong aftershocks in the same area, of magnitude 5.6 and 5.9.
Indonesia’s Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) warned of the possibility of tsunami waves being generated by the quake.
Indonesia and neighbouring countries experience frequent earthquakes due to their location in the Pacific “Ring of Fire” -- an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin.

stories.headline: Deflating the wind in the willows
stories.deck: Kashmir’s famed ₹700-crore bat-making industry supports at least 50,000 livelihoods. Since 2021, its bats have made their way to cricket grounds around the world, with 47 international players using Kashmir willow bats in major tournaments. But a shortage of willow, climate change, and smuggling are putting the industry under pressure. Peerzada Ashiq reports on its rise and the challenges…
stories.bodyText:
In Halmulla in south Kashmir’s Anantnag district, larger-than-life pictures of cricket stars such as Sachin Tendulkar, Virat Kohil, M.S. Dhoni, Shahid Afridi, and Babar Azam line the bat shops on National Highway-44.
Fawzul Kabiir, 40, founder of GR8 Sports, is busy inspecting the English willow clefts neatly stacked into a 12-foot-high tower. Clefts, or wedge-shaped blocks of willow wood cut from timber, are turned into bats and customised to meet the evolving demands of cricket.
While displaying different bars, Kabiir says, “A bat used by an opener is different from that which is used by a middle-order batsman and a slogger. Bats used for one-day matches are different from those used in the T20 format. Each player has a preference of his own.”
The craftsmanship of local bat-makers comes into play in producing bats sturdy enough to endure wallops or dents, even after being hit by a leather ball. “Seasons are important in maintaining the uniqueness of the bat. We allow the willow clefts to brave the rain and snow in the open. Sun-dried clefts are the best to compete in international markets,” Kabiir explains.
Inside his well-equipped bat factory, Kabiir tosses a ball into the air and lets it fall onto a bat, listening to the sound to check for the “sweet spot”. “It’s a science I mastered after my bats faced rejection in many countries in 2010, when I showcased some of my samples,” he explains. “Our bats would not meet international standards. And just as we began producing international-quality bats, we have been hit by a shortage of raw material.”
Famous for its mountain slopes, lush meadows and clear streams, Kashmir enjoys another reputation: the craftsmanship of its bat-makers. According to government data, Kashmir has 195 registered bat manufacturers, mainly in south Kashmir, and around 150 cleft dealers. They shape willow planks into sturdy, beautiful bats that find their way to cricket grounds around the world.
This international fame came only in 2021, when a bat-making company from Kashmir was certified by the International Cricket Council (ICC) and bagged a contract to supply bats to the Oman Cricket Board. However, it was during the Cricket World Cup 2022 that the Kashmir willow made it to the spotlight when UAE player Junaid Siddique hit the longest six of 109 meters off a Sri Lankan bowler, Dushmantha Chameera.
The industry is also an important source of livelihood in the region, for at least 50,000 locals. However, it is now grappling with several issues, including shortage of raw material, changes in climate, and smuggling.
A growing industry
The Kashmir willow is a deciduous tree native to Europe and western Asia. It was brought to the Kashmir Valley during British rule in 1895 by British officials Sir Walter R. Lawrence and J.C. MacDonell, the first chief of the Forest Department in Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), to meet fuel needs and provide green fodder for cattle.
According to Yaseer Ahmad Mir, Assistant Professor at the National Institute of Fashion Technology, Salix alba, a species of English willow, was also introduced to make cricket bats, as it was difficult for the British to export bats from England. “They found the climatic conditions of Kashmir suitable for making these bats,” he says.
The willow wood is usually sourced from areas surrounding Anantnag. English willow trees are harvested after 12-15 years of growth, or when they attain a girth of 120 cm at 1.5 metres above the ground and stand about 12 metres tall. They are then cut into blocks or clefts and left to dry under the sun for months.
The wood is hard-wearing, relatively light, and easy to sand and shape. “The quality of willow is improved by drying and pressing it during its production stage,” says Mir.
According to data from the Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Agriculture and Science Technology, a mature willow tree with a girth of 100 centimetres produces about 15-20 willow clefts. Accordingly, around 1.2 lakh mature Salix trees are felled to produce 30 lakh cricket bats per year. This is double the number manufactured a decade ago.
Kabiir says 47 international players have used Kashmir willow bats in international tournaments, including the ICC T20 World Cups in 2021 and 2022 and the ODI World Cup in 2023. They include India’s Munaf Patel, Yusuf Pathan, and Wasim Jaffer; Pakistan’s Mohammad Yousuf; Bangladesh’s Saqib Al Hasan, and West Indies’ Kusal Perera and Chris Gayle.
He says: “We have not only made cricket bats lighter, but also ensured that the ping, balance, and stroke is matchless.”
In the 2024 ICC Women’s T20 World Cup, West Indies players Aaliyah Alleyne, Zaida James, and Shamilia Connell wrote a new chapter in Kashmir’s bat-making story by using the bats made in the region for the first time. Kabiir says that achieving this feat in women’s cricket required bat manufacturers to undergo a series of tests. The tests assessed lighter bat weights and sweet spots at multiple points on the blade, based on the preferences of the women cricketers.
Kabiir says the bats are affordable compared to those produced elsewhere. “Compared to English willow bats from the U.K. that cost ₹1.5 lakh-2 lakh, the bats produced here range from ₹300 to ₹20,000. This makes them much more affordable. States such as Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, West Bengal, and Delhi queue up with orders for bats every year,” he says.
The plan to tackle the quality crisis
However, just as it was growing towards the ₹700-crore mark and deepening its roots in international cricket, Kashmir’s bat-making industry is struggling to meet both domestic and international orders, Kabiir says. The price of English willow is an indicator of the shortage: per foot, it has gone up from ₹300 in 2021 to ₹1,250. “The Jammu and Kashmir (J&K) government needs to step in to bridge the gap and help the bat industry here expand,” he says.
Javed Ahmed Rana, the Forest Minister of J&K, agrees that the declining availability of quality willow timber is one of the biggest challenges confronting the cricket bat industry in the Union Territory. To tackle the shortage, “a coordinated drive is in place to revive willow cultivation across Kashmir,” he says.
According to the Forest Department, the government plans to plant 1,100 willow trees per hectare across 200 hectares of forest and State land, with a target of 2.2 lakh trees starting this year. The move could help the bat industry increase production to 50 lakh bats per year.
According to Rana, the J&K government is identifying “suitable low-lying and marshy areas across the Valley for expanding willow plantations”. It has roped in the State Forest Research Institute to introduce improved willow species and clones to enhance both productivity and sustainability. He says the government needs to build a self-sustaining willow cultivation ecosystem through scientific management, quality planting material, identifying new plantation areas, and greater farmer participation.
In 1917, the Forest Department under the Dogra rulers, identified alluvial and riparian willow species and planted them along rivers, stream banks, and point bars. Wetland willows were also planted in areas with saturated soils, including around the wetlands of Wular Lake, Harran, Hygam, Hokur-sur, Mirgund, Mamandangi, Gund Jehangir, and Shahgund. An official estimate suggests that about 5 million willow trees existed in and around these areas.
Irfan Ali Shah, Conservator of Forests, North Circle, says the Forest Department at present manages approximately 67 hectares of land under willow plantations. “These plantations are managed scientifically according to approved working plans under the Willow Plantation Working Circle. Sites are selected based on soil moisture, drainage, water availability, productivity, and the ecological needs of the species,” he says.
English willow is particularly suited to mildly waterlogged and moisture-retentive areas, “where adequate soil moisture can support satisfactory growth during its rotation period”. Besides south Kashmir, Baramulla, Kupwara, and Bandipora are also emerging as hubs of willow cultivation.
“The Lidder Forest Division in Bijbehara plans to plant English willow cuttings in available open spaces in the Momandanji and Katriteng plantations, covering about 5 hectares. The initiative aims to expand the existing willow resource and promote scientific regeneration in suitable areas,” says Shah.
Changes in weather patters
Changes in climatic conditions too are adding to the industry’s woes. Nazir Dar, a bat manufacturer from Bijbehara, says many wetlands around local springs have dried up in the past five years. “Springs would feed water bodies and allow willows to grow thick and tall. The construction of houses and the entry of waste, especially polythene, into water bodies have choked scores of springs in Anantnag district,” he says.
Shah too admits that this is a challenge but adds that the situation is under control. “The availability of adequate moisture is an important factor governing the growth and establishment of willow, particularly in areas traditionally associated with wetland or waterlogged conditions. The drying of wetlands or their degradation as well as reduction in water availability can all adversely affect willow regeneration,” he says.
However, he is quick to add that it would be inappropriate to state that wetlands in south Kashmir have completely stopped supporting English willow cultivation solely because of drying of water bodies. “In some locations, declining water levels or changes in hydrology may have reduced the suitability of certain sites for new plantations or natural regeneration,” says Shah.
He says changing climatic patterns could have an impact on English willow particularly because it is closely associated with adequate soil moisture and water availability. The changes in temperature, precipitation patterns, and duration of dry periods events may influence the growth, establishment, and productivity of willow plantations.
“However, it would be prudent not to attribute any observed decline in willow exclusively to climate change without systematic field-based evidence. The observed changes may also be influenced by land use changes, water body degradation, harvesting practices, plantation management, and availability of suitable planting material,” he adds.
Problem of smuggling
Smuggling remains another challenge to the industry in Kashmir.
After the dilution of Article 370 in 2019 by the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Central government, the Jammu and Kashmir Willow (Prohibition on Export and Movement) Act, 2000, was just one of the two local laws retained to “to curb smuggling of willow clefts”.
“Kashmir willow timber is being smuggled to places such as Jalandhar and Meerut, which have their own bat-making units and flourishing export industries,” says Mir.
Until the mid-1970s, Kashmir willow wood was transported to various manufacturing units across India. “But when the J&K government realised the importance of the willow wood and the potential of the industry in Kashmir, it restricted the number of clefts that could be sold outside. After the ban, the smuggling of willow increased. Locals claim that over 25 lakh clefts are smuggled every year,” Mir adds.
English willow timber is harvested twice a year in May and September. Kabiir says he goes to private willow tree fields in Ganderbal and Kupwara every year in the spring and identifies the female species of English willow by monitoring the movement of pollinators. “The willow trees with flowers are the female species. They are light weight, flexible and without knots, and have a good shine. It is this species that allows us to produce Grade A bats of international standard and fetches us the highest profit.”
But access to good-quality timber remains a challenge. With the inconsistent quality of timber denting its reputation in the domestic market, the Geographical Indication (GI) tag in 2025 has come as a shot in the arm for the bat industry.
Mir was one of the members of the committee that prepared the dossier report for the GI tag of the Kashmir willow bat. “The GI recognition gives Kashmir willow bats additional value. It is also a strong marketing tool that can help expand their reach and increase their prices,” explains Mir.

briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Paving the way for Tamil Nadu govt to grant jobs to family members of those who died in the Karur stampede last year, SC Friday stayed operation of Madras HC’s verdict that had quashed the govt decision.
Asking what was wrong if a govt provided succour to a deceased’s family, an SC bench agreed to hear an appeal filed by the state govt against the HC order.
The court issued notice on the govt’s plea and stayed the HC order. HC had said if compassionate appointment was permitted in the present case, it would open the floodgates for various others to seek such employment.

Lord's to Lahore: A look at India's milestone Tests before the 600th at Galle
briefs.deck: The men-in-Blue, led by Shubman Gill, are set to become only the third team after England and Australia to reach the milestone, that too on the day when the nation is celebrating its 80th Independence Day from the colonial rule..
briefs.bodyText:
Ninety-four years after Colonel Cottari Kanakaiya Nayudu (CK Nayadu) led a motley crew of a resurgent nation in their first Test match at Lord's Cricket Ground on June 25 1932, India will play their 600th game in the cricket's oldest and toughest format at Galle International Stadium in Sri Lanka on Saturday.
The men-in-Blue, led by Shubman Gill, are set to become only the third team after England and Australia to reach the milestone, that too on the day when the nation is celebrating its 80th Independence Day from the colonial rule.
A total of 319 lucky players have donned the India cap in Tests so far, Manav Suthar being the latest among them, and Sachin Tendulkar holds the record of most Test caps - 200.
From Colonel C K Nayadu to Rishabh Pant, Indian men's cricket team have been led by 38 captains in these ninety-four years, under whom they have been through the lowest of lows to the highest of highs but constantly aspiring to be better.
Virat Kohli holds the record for captaining India in the most Test matches, having led the team in 68 Tests from 2014 to 2022. Under his leadership, India secured 40 wins, making him also India's most successful Test captain.
As India are set to create history at Galle, here’s a look at India’s 1st, 100th, 200th, 300th, 400th nd 500th match:
India's first Test: England vs India, Lord's, June 25 - 28, 1932
The Maharajah of Porbandar was named captain of the touring Indian side but good sense prevailed and CK Nayadu was nominated to lead the side in India's first-ever Test, however not before some off-field drama.
England captain Douglas Jardine rescued his side after Mohammad Nissar rocked England as he clean bowled Percy Holmes and Herbert Sutcliffe, on 6 and 3, respectively.
Jardine's 79 and Les Ames' 65 took England to 259 in the first innings. Nasser (93/5) took India's first five-wicket haul in Tests.
India were bowled out for 189 in their first innings as Bill Bowes (49/4) and Bill Voice (23/3) ran through Indian batting, giving England a lead of 70 runs, which they capitalized on, and declared their second innings at 275/8.
India had 346 runs to chase and England easily won the match by 158 runs despite Amar Singh's (51) gutsy knock.
India's 100th Test: India vs England, Birmingham, July 13 - 15, 1967
Led by one of India's greatest Test captain, Mansur Ali Khan Pataudi, India toured England England for a three-match Test series.
Having lost the first two Tests, India entered the third match looking to avoid a series whitewash.
England won the toss and scored 298 in the first innings. India's four spinners — Srinivas Venkataraghavan, Bhagwath Chandrasekhar, Bishan Bedi and Erapalli Prasanna — took all 10 English wickets.
India's batting line-up featured Farokh Engineer, Ajit Wadekar, Chandu Borde and Pataudi, but the visitors struggled against the England attack. India were bowled out for just 92, with only four batters reaching double figures. Engineer was the top scorer with 23.
Chandrasekhar, Bedi and Prasanna then took nine of England's 10 second-innings wickets. However, England had already built a lead of more than 400 and set India a target of 410.
Wadekar scored 70, but India were dismissed for 277. England won by 132 runs and completed a 3-0 series sweep.
India's 200th Test: India vs Pakistan, Lahore,  December 10 - 15, 1982
Their was no Covid-19 in 1982, but there were no spectators in Lahore's historic Gaddafi Stadium to see the Test match as the Pakistan Cricket Board - then Board of Control for Cricket in Pakistan (BCCP), had sold the entire series to a private party for around £800,000. The contractor set high entry prices, keeping many spectators away. The rates were cut by half after the second day, but the crowds did not return.
The match, first of the six-Test series, had some terrific performances from batsmen of both sides. Zaheer Abbas played a monstrous knock of 215 runs, which was also his 100th first class ton, as Pakistan finished their first innings at 485, after being asked to bat by Indian captain Sunil Gavaskar.
Returning to the side after nearly two years, Mohinder Amarnath led India's reply with an unbeaten knock of 109 runs. Sunil Gavaskar also scored 81, and passed the 7,000 Test run mark, while Sandeep Patil played a quickfire knock of 68 off 56 balls. India scored 379 in their first innings.
Pakistan scored 135/1 in their second innings, and the match ended in a draw.
India's 300th Test: India vs South Africa, Ahmedabad, November 20 - 23, 1996
It was the first Test of the three-match series against South Africa, and VVS Laxman also made his Test debut in this match. India captain Sachin Tendulkar put India into advantagious position by batting first on a brown, dusty pitch.
Tendulkar's 42, Manjrekar's 34, Azharuddin's 35 helped India reach 223 in their first innings even as Allan Donald took 37 for 4.
India however hit back with spin and the then trio of Anil Kumble, Sunil Joshi and Narendra Hirwani scalped 8 South African wickets, and South Africa could take just 21-run lead.
India struggled again with the bat and were reduced to 123/6 in their second innings. Laxman scored 51 and helped India reach 190.
South Africa needed 170 to win but lost two wickets without adding a run to the scoreboard. Javagal Srinath then took six wickets as South Africa were bowled out for 105.
India's 400th Test: West Indies vs India, Sabina Park, Jamaica, June 30 - July 02, 2006
All previous three of the Tests in the series had ended in a draw and both teams reached Sabina Park for the last Test.
Brian Charles Lara's side were bundled out for a mere 103 with Harbhajan Singh (13/5) being the wrecker-in-chief.
Rahul Dravid, India's captain, won the toss and chose to bat. India struggled with the bat again, but Dravid scored 81 as they made 200.
India had a 97-run lead but could not build a big advantage with the bat. Dravid again led the way, scoring 68 as India were dismissed for 171. West Indies were set 269 to win. Anil Kumble took six wickets as India bowled them out for 219.
India won by 49 runs in their 400th Test.
India's 500th Test: India vs New Zealand, Green Park, Kanpur
India reached Kanpur's iconic Green Park stadium to play the 500th Test, led by Virat Kohli. It was the first Test of three-match series.
The Test match was being played at the time when India were at peak of their home domination with Ashiwn and Jadeja at their best. Murali Vijay (65), and Cheteshwar Pujara's (62) half-centuries took India to 318 in the first innings on a decent pitch.
While Tom Latham (58), New Zealand captain Kane Williamson (75), and Luke Ronchi (38) played promising knocks as Black Caps batted for almost 96 overs, Jadeja (73/5), and Ashwin (93/4) made sure India had a lead of 56 runs.
Four Indian batters - Vijay, Pujara, Rohit Sharma, and Jadeja - scored fifties in the second innings as India declared at 377/5 on day 4, setting an improbable target of 434 runs for New Zealand.
Of course Ravichandran Ashwin finished the job in the fourth innings, taking a six-wicket haul, and India scripted a famous win by 197 runs at Green Park.
India went on to win the series 3-0.

stories.headline: Couple found dead at their house in Bengaluru’s Rajagopalnagar
stories.bodyText:
A 32-year-old man and his wife were found dead at their house under suspicious circumstances in northwest Bengaluru’s Rajagopalnagar on Friday, police said.
The deceased have been identified as Sumanth Jain, a native of Dakshina Kannada, and his 28-year-old wife, Padmavathi. The couple had been married for over three years and had been residing in a rented house near Hegganahalli for the past four months.
According to the police, the couple allegedly had a fight over a marital issue on Thursday night, which escalated and might have ended with Jain killing his wife and subsequently reportedly taking his own life out of fear of the consequences.
The incident came to light when Jain’s relatives arrived at his house. An investigator in the case told The Hindu that Jain had sent a voice message to his mother on Friday at 1.30 a.m., saying that he was taking his life and that she could take his belongings. However, the mother checked the phone later in the day and tried to call him multiple times.
“All calls to him went unanswered, prompting Jain’s mother to call a relative to check on her son. When they went to his house on Friday evening, the incident came to light and we were informed subsequently,” the officer said.
The officer noted that the police are yet to establish how he allegedly killed his wife and what the trigger point was. Police have sent both bodies for post-mortem, and the exact cause of death will only be known after the report is received. They have also not ruled out the possibility of self-harm by both.
For now, Rajagopalnagar police have registered an FIR under Section 103 of the BNS, which deals with murder. In addition, an Unnatural Death Report (UDR) has also been filed.
According to the police, Jain worked as a civil engineer at a company in Nandini Layout, while Padmavathi also worked as an engineer at a company in east Bengaluru’s Whitefield. The bodies of the deceased will be handed over to their families after the post-mortem.

stories.headline: Deck of kings: Bengaluru teen’s card game makes history lessons fun
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Tired of memorising names and dates from history textbooks? A class 10 student Sinchana S from Bengaluru has designed a card game, featuring 50 Indian rulers to make learning more engaging for children.
Inspired by Pokemon trading cards, 15-year-old Sinchana developed a deck that is based on rulers featured in NCERT textbooks from Classes 7 to 10. Each card assigns scores for attributes such as military power, welfare, wealth and historical impact, allowing players to compete by comparing strengths of rulers, ranging from Ashoka and Krishnadevaraya to Shivaji Maharaj.
The idea struck her while watching friends effortlessly recall details of hundreds of Pokémon characters. “With one game, children could remember so many Pokémon. I wondered why we couldn’t learn history the same way,” she said.
What began as a simple idea in Nov last year evolved into months-long project, involving multiple redesigns, play-testing sessions and feedback from friends, cousins and teachers. Using Canva and AI tools to create the visuals, she revised the deck nearly six times before finalising it in May this year.
The game has already been introduced in her school, where history teachers encouraged students to play it during class. She also distributed around 170 card sets to BBMP schools, personally demonstrating the game to students. “The goal is not to make children memorise facts but to spark curiosity. If they come across a ruler in the game and later, want to know more about them, the game has done its job,” she said.
A history enthusiast since childhood, Sinchana credits family trips to historical sites such as Hampi, Badami, Pattadakal and the Shore Temple, along with stories narrated by her father, for nurturing her interest in the subject. The family has so far printed about 200 sets of the laminated cards.
Interestingly, the teenager is already working on her next idea — a finance-themed educational game aimed at helping students understand saving, investing and personal finance. “I love finance and I might also perceive it in my higher studies. Now after these cards, I am exploring if I can do something to simply finance and understand finance better,” she said.
Sinchana’s efforts were recently recognised by Bengaluru West City Corporation, which sent her an appreciation letter for developing an innovative learning tool after she donated cards to govt schools. While the family is exploring ways to expand its reach, Sinchana’s father Santosh Kumar said the primary goal remains educational. “We want more students to enjoy learning history.”

stories.headline: Dog dispute turns violent, woman assaulted in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A dispute over a stray dog being pelted with stones escalated into a heated confrontation and alleged assault on a 27-year-old woman in Domlur on Aug 10.
According to a complaint filed by 
Sanjana
 (name changed), the incident occurred around 7.40pm when she was standing outside her house in Domlur I Stage and speaking to a neighbour. They noticed a person deliberately throwing stones at a stray dog on the street. When they questioned him, the dog and two others barked and ran towards a girl standing outside a nearby house, frightening her and making her cry.
Even as Sanjana rushed towards the child, her family members came out of the house. At this point, another resident allegedly shouted twice, “Sampeyyanda kukkal nee” (‘kill the dogs’ in Telugu), allegedly inciting those present. Following the provocation, two members of the girl’s family picked up stones and chased the dogs away.
The situation then allegedly turned into a confrontation with Sanjana. She claimed that 4-5 members of the family surrounded her and argued with her. An elderly man allegedly approached her, blocked her way, and verbally abused her despite her repeatedly asking him to maintain distance. The man allegedly pushed her hard, after which she immediately called the police helpline.
Based on her complaint, police registered a case for voluntarily causing hurt, criminal intimidation and wrongful restraint.

stories.headline: Woman’s death in Bengaluru accident becomes flashpoint for residents’ anger over bad roads in Electronics City Phase 2
stories.deck: Following Medha Prithviraj’s death, residents have been demanding better roads in Electronics City Phase 1. While most roads in the area are narrow and pothole-filled, several other stretches have been dug up for civic works.
stories.bodyText:
The protest that erupted after a 32-year-old woman died in a road accident in Electronics City Phase 2 is an outcome of years of anger against the municipal administration, as local residents have consistently been protesting over poor road infrastructure in the area.
About 400 people participated in a candlelight protest against the administration after Medha Prithviraj, a resident of the area, was run over by a small goods vehicle on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).
According to the police, Medha was pillion-riding on a two-wheeler with her friend on their way to the office when the incident unfolded near the Venkateshwara Temple arch in Ananth Nagar. The driver reportedly applied the brakes to avoid a crash as the vehicle in front also applied sudden brakes. The two-wheeler allegedly skidded, causing both to fall. The rider narrowly escaped, but a goods vehicle coming from the opposite direction ran over Medha, killing her on the spot.
As officers from the municipal administration, Bengaluru city police, and traffic police gathered near the temple arch, residents poured in with questions and demanded accountability. This resulted in a chaotic exchange, prompting the officials to leave the place.
‘Braking caused accident’
Later, the municipal administration claimed that the accident was not an outcome of a bad road but was instead caused by the application of immediate brakes, stressing that the stretch had been recently asphalted.
A source in the traffic police told The Hindu that CUT FOR PRINT even the complainant in the case, the person who was driving the two-wheeler, had also said that he had applied the brakes to avoid a crash.
The officer, however, admitted that the accident was a flashpoint, as the protesters were actually demanding better roads. TILL HERE several stretches are dug up around the locality for civic works, and most roads in the area are narrow.
OPTIONAL FOR PRINT The Hindu, in December, had reported on the infrastructure collapse in the exact locality and surrounding areas. TILL HERE
Poor infrastruture
The area suffers from poorly developed facilities. The connecting roads are either muddy or filled with large craters, and garbage lies strewn around. While a few roads have been taken up for works, the area still suffers from poor infrastructure.

Residents demand better roads

briefs.headline: Parking permit move sparks backlash, fears of higher rent in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Greater Bengaluru Authority’s proposal to collect annual fee from owners of vehicles parked on roads in front of their house has triggered a wave of backlash. Citizens slammed the proposal, saying it unfairly penalises vehicle owners for decades of poor urban planning and hinting that tenants may have to bear higher monthly rentals.
The draft notification released on Thursday plans to collect an annual fee of Rs 15,000 for hatchbacks, Rs 20,000 for sedans and Rs 25,000 from SUVs.
The proposal has raised more questions than answers, particularly in older residential neighbourhoods where houses were built long before the rapid rise in vehicle ownership and without adequate parking provisions. “For a majority of those who come to Bengaluru to make a living, a second-hand car is an aspiration. But the govt is hitting us by imposing a parking fee, this is unfair,” a resident said.
Owners of independent residential buildings fear the additional cost will eventually be passed on to tenants, making rents more expensive for families owning cars.
Many residents questioned the rationale behind charging a fee without offering assurance on vehicle safety. A senior GBA official clarified that a parking permit would not guarantee the safety of vehicles parked on public roads.
Residents SpeakShiv Kumar V, general secretary, Domlur Layout RWA: For older residential buildings, it’s impractical. These homes were built decades ago and owners cannot suddenly create additional parking space. This will directly impact the middle class. Instead of burdening residents with annual parking permit fees, authorities should first act against commercial buildings that have converted basements meant for parking into business spaces.
Abhijit MS, Kasturinagar: The regulation is needed because for years people have treated roads and footpaths as free parking spaces. However, it cannot be implemented as a blanket policy across all roads. The government should have introduced reforms at the vehicle registration stage by ensuring buyers have access to parking before purchasing a vehicle.
Raghu Rajgopalan, Koramangala 4th Block RWA:
 Residents are already paying road tax and now asking them to pay Rs 15,000 annually to park on their own street, without any guarantee of safety, is unreasonable. Before imposing parking permits, the government must improve public transport connectivity and create adequate parking infrastructure.
SG Aditya, general secretary, Indiranagar Owner Traders & Residents Welfare Assn:
 This is daylight robbery. If a household owns two cars, it could end up paying nearly Rs 60,000 a year in parking permit fees. The policy must undergo scrutiny.
Anil Kumar Janardanan, Jalahalli West resident: The introduction of yearly permits has a downside. We can request police to get the parked vehicles removed to facilitate easy movement during peak hours. If they are given a permit, they will not move their vehicles at all.
Ajay Kumar C, Swayam Jagruthi NGO and Nagarbhavi resident: When mandatory parking on many commercial stretches near residential areas is not being enforced, bringing a host of new regulations makes no sense.
Guruprasad Rotti, Heritage Basavanagudi Residents Welfare Forum: The policy helps deal with parking mafia, wherein commercial establishments like hotels get several slots blocked for their own customers instead of providing parking on their premises.
Dhruv N Koundinya, citizen: The first question: Who approved buildings? The policy discourages private vehicles in favour of public transportation. However, when we are being charged for parking or being levied high penalties, we must be provided with good public transport service as an alternative solution.

briefs.headline: ‘Madonna and Child’ coming to Bengaluru museum
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 The consulate general of Italy in Bengaluru, in collaboration with National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), Bengaluru and ministry of culture, will host “One mother, many mother tongues”, an exhibition featuring masterpieces from Italy and India.
The exhibition is from Aug 20-Sept 20 at the National Gallery of Modern Art, Bengaluru.
It will trace the evolving representations of motherhood across cultures and centuries. A highlight is Sandro Botticelli’s Madonna and Child (c. 1490), which will be presented in India for the first time.
The painting will offer art lovers a rare opportunity to encounter one of the greatest masters of Renaissance alongside ancient Etruscan sculptures in marble, schist, sandstone and terracotta. Among the Indian works to be presented is a Kushan-period Hariti from Mathura museum.
The exhibition will also bring together masterpieces from lesser-known sites and provincial museums, including a sculpture of Skandamata from a remote temple of Thaneshwar near Udaipur.
From Italy, a group of ancient Etruscan images of Mater Matuta -- the protector goddess of children and a symbol of dawn, renewal and regeneration -- will be presented.
“The exhibition represents an important milestone in the cultural dialogue between Italy and India as we look ahead to India-Italy year of culture and tourism. This exhibition celebrates the deep and diverse connections between our two civilisations..” said Giandomenico Milano, consul general of Italy in Bengaluru.

briefs.headline: Egg attacks target Kerala buses near Bidadi? Karnataka cops deny link with fatal accident
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A week after a fatal accident in Bidadi involving a Kerala State Road Transport Corporation bus, a second bus survived another mishap along the same stretch of Bengaluru-Mysuru expressway. The Kerala bus, coming from Kasaragod, encountered an egg attack while it was crossing Bidadi around 9.30pm Wednesday.
The bus driver stopped the vehicle as there was no visibility through the windowpanes as egg white blocked his vision. Following the incident, the driver filed a complaint with Bidadi police station. “We are taking legal advice before proceeding with the FIR,” a cop said.
Local activists claim that egg-throwing at Kerala buses is “not an isolated incident,” with those who visited the fatal accident site claiming there were remains of egg shells along the wreckage.
Karnataka police have denied any link between egg-throwing and the Kerala bus accident that left a driver and a conductor dead last week.
In a petition to Karnataka’s home and transport ministers, Shihab Thangal Centre For Humanity, a city-based NGO, stated that a series of alarming criminal activities had occurred on the Bengaluru-Mysuru expressway, specifically targeting Kerala buses. “It is deeply concerning that this incident occurred in the same vicinity where a fatal accident involving a KSRTC bus recently resulted in the loss of lives of a driver and a conductor.
 We fear that these deliberate acts may be part of a larger criminal strategy,” MK Noushad, general secretary of the organisation, said.
Kerala transport minister CP John stated that a probe has been ordered to find out the cause of the egg hurling.

briefs.headline: Proposed parking charges a solution or a price on Bengaluru’s traffic problem?
briefs.bodyText:
Will the proposed draft parking policy actually ease congestion or just put a price on a problem the city has failed to address for years?
While transport experts argue that parking charges must “discourage” owners from parking their vehicles in congested areas, others argue that levying parking charges without fixing public infrastructure makes citizens pay for a problem that governments helped create.
Demand management
For professor and convenor of the IISc Sustainable Transportation Lab (IST Lab) Ashish Verma, the biggest mistake would be to approach the policy as a way of meeting the city’s demand for parking. The objective should be to reduce the demand for private vehicles in places that are already congested, he said.
“The idea should not be to assess the demand for parking in different areas and accordingly provide adequate supply for parking,” he said. The solution is to make parking restrictive in the city’s most congested areas- both by reducing available spaces and making parking more expensive, particularly during peak periods, he said, arguing that parking should be used “as a demand management measure”.
While restricting cars immediately raises the question of what happens to the people who currently depend on them, that alternative, Prof. Verma said, has to be built alongside the parking policy rather than after it.
Disincentivise multiple car buyers
Dattaraya Devare, an environmental activist who has been championing paid parking, believes the price itself can influence vehicle ownership and use.
“Residential parking could be pricier, but it can be managed by introducing fee slabs based on the particular period when the car was bought. The move will disincentivise people from owning multiple cars,” he said.
Alternatives
But that argument assumes residents have enough choice to respond to the price. Srikanth Narasimhan, founder and general secretary of the Bengaluru Navanirmana Party (BNP), argues that this is what Bengaluru lacks.
Mr. Narasimhan opposed the proposed parking charges based on the premise that the government needs to first provide citizens with real alternatives and take responsibility for the parking crisis.
“While parking charges are not inherently wrong, charging citizens for parking without alternatives is unfair. What choice does a citizen have when public transport is still inadequate?” he questioned, pointing out to the delayed suburban rail, the limited growth of the BMTC fleet, weak last-mile connectivity, delays in metro projects and poor footpaths.
Lack of space
There is also a question of how the existing residential parking system can be regulated at all.
N.S. Mukunda, founder-member of Bengaluru Praja Vedike, said residents may actually be willing to pay for permits if doing so guarantees them a designated space and eliminates the daily disputes over who can park on a particular stretch of road.
“Many disputes arise over parking spaces on streets, so if the authorities allot designated parking spaces on the road, those who want to avoid such hassles will easily obtain a permit,” he said.
But that immediately creates another problem- where will these spaces come from? Bengaluru has very little vacant land available for large-scale off-street parking, and Mr. Mukunda said this could make the policy extremely difficult to implement.
Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok called the policy as a “new sketch of looting government”, arguing that the proposed GBA parking rules would make residents pay ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 a year to park their cars on the road in front of their homes.
“Rows of potholes, roads that turn into swimming pools when it rains, what moral right does a government that is incapable of fixing them have to collect this parking tax?” he asked.

briefs.headline: Parking rates may double on Bengaluru’s busiest commercial stretches under draft rules
briefs.bodyText:
If the Karnataka government notifies the draft Greater Bengaluru Authority (Parking) Rules, 2026, the fee for parking in commercial hubs such as M.G. Road and Brigade Road will likely increase by more than twofold from the current charges.
The draft rules, published on August 11, mandate city corporations to categorise all stretches into three types. Type A, defined as a commercial road that attracts people from across the city, will have a higher charge structure.
There are several such stretches in Bengaluru, including Kalyan Nagar Main Road, Sampige Road, Lavelle Road, Koramangala Main Road, and Indiranagar’s 80 Feet and 100 Feet roads, among others.
According to the suggested parking fee structure, two-wheelers and cars along such stretches will be charged ₹40 per hour. For off-street parking, two-wheelers will have to pay ₹20 per hour, while four-wheelers will have to pay ₹40 per hour.
In contrast, the current parking fee on several stretches that qualify as Category A is nominal, at ₹15 per hour for two-wheelers and ₹30 for cars. even for off-street parking, the fee will see a 33.3% increase.
The increase will be a financial burden for several office-goers, especially those who have offices in Central Bengaluru. Due to a lack of space and the dominance of commercial establishments, several offices do not have parking spaces, forcing employees to use on-street parking.
Navya R., a resident of north Bengaluru who commutes to central Bengaluru, says that without the mass expansion of public transport, bringing in such a system will be a huge financial burden.
“To create off-street parking, there is a severe dearth of land in central Bengaluru. So, what will commuters do?” she questioned.
A source who was part of the consultant departments for the policy explained that the rationale behind hiking the price is to minimise on-street parking to a greater extent on arterial and sub-arterial roads. “If parking can be limited on such major roads, the result will have a positive impact on commute times. When off-street parking expands and the demand for on-street parking shifts towards the former, it will have a greater impact,” the official opined.

briefs.headline: Karnataka to introduce Command and Control Centre as part of measures to stop pilferage of PDS supplies
briefs.bodyText:
In order to prevent the pilferage of ration food grains, Karnataka is planning a seamless system including a CCTV cameras in godowns, GPS systems in vehicles that transport the PDS supplies and Command and Control Centre to monitor it all.
“The contractors concerned have been instructed to install GPS in all vehicles transporting ration grains. The Karnataka Food and Civil Supplies Corporation (KFCSC) has been instructed to install CCTVs in the KSCSC and non-KFCSC godowns. The tender process is under way to set up a Command and Control Centre in the department,” said Rizwan Arshad, Minister for Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs of Karnataka, addressing the media.
“We have technology. So why not use it,” Mr. Arshad said, adding that the new features are part of the effort to introduce a permanent solution to the problem.
Smart revamp
The department has been trying to revamp the PDS distribution through a ‘smart PDS’ system where an ePoS machine to verify the credentials of the beneficiary and an electronic weighing machine to accurately measure the quantity they are eligible for are proposed. The tender process for the installation of the same is in progress, the Minister said.
According to Mr. Arshad, as many as 1,497 FIRs have been registered in the last three years in connection with pilferage of PDS supply with 86,181 quintals of food grains and supplies worth ₹49.38 crores seized.
Deletion of BPL cards paused
As per government data, currently 4,44,32,102 beneficiaries in the State are covered under the PDS scheme.
Mr. Arshad said the Central government had provided a list of 7,76,206 people suspected to be ineligible for BPL cards. Following this, 4,26,835 ration cards have been converted into APL.
“We have stayed further deletions temporarily for now. However, as per the law we have to ultimately heed to the Central government and cannot act independently,” he said.
Regarding the Indira Food Kit scheme for the BPL card holders, the Minister noted that the department is further analysing it as the price of essentials have gone up due to the ongoing war.

stories.headline: Forex kitty jumps $14.14 billion to $707 billion in one of the biggest weekly expansions
stories.deck: The overall kitty had jumped by $10.512 billion to $692.866 billion in the previous reporting week ended July 31
stories.bodyText:
India's forex reserves jumped $14.136 billion to $707.002 billion during the week ended August 7, the Reserve Bank said on Friday (August 14, 2026).
The overall kitty had jumped by $10.512 billion to $692.866 billion in the previous reporting week ended July 31.
The reserves had expanded to an all-time high of $728.494 billion during the week ended February 27 this year before the onset of the West Asia conflict that led to several weeks of drop as the rupee came under pressure and the RBI had to intervene in the forex market through dollar sales.
For the week ended August 7, foreign currency assets, a major component of the reserves, increased $9.946 billion to $574.625 billion, the central bank's data showed.
Expressed in dollar terms, the foreign currency assets include effects of appreciation or depreciation of non-U.S. units, such as the euro, pound, and yen, held in foreign exchange reserves.
It can be recalled that the central bank and the government had in July launched a series of measures, including the FCNR(B) scheme, to attract more forex flows into the country. The country has so far received $40 billion under the schemes, as per reports.
Value of gold reserves increased $3.995 billion to $108.738 billion during the week, the RBI said.
The special drawing rights (SDRs) were up $79 million at $18.745 billion, the apex bank said.
India's reserve position with the IMF was also up by $116 million to $4.894 billion at the end of the reporting week, according to the apex bank's data.

stories.headline: Current account deficit widens to $6.2 billion in Jun: RBI data
stories.deck: The current account deficit was primarily driven by a widening merchandise trade deficit, which rose to $30.2 billion in June 2026 from $19.2 billion a year earlier
stories.bodyText:
India's current account deficit widened to $6.2 billion in June from a surplus of $1.2 billion in the year-ago month, according to preliminary data released by the Reserve Bank of India on Friday (August 14, 2026).
The current account deficit was primarily driven by a widening merchandise trade deficit, which rose to $30.2 billion in June 2026 from $19.2 billion a year earlier.
Merchandise exports increased to $41.2 billion in June from $35.3 billion in the year-ago month, while imports rose at a faster pace to $71.4 billion from $54.5 billion.
The data from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) also showed that the surplus in services increased to $17.9 billion in June 2026 from $16.2 billion a year earlier.
Services exports rose to $36.4 billion from $32.1 billion, while imports increased to $18.5 billion from $15.9 billion.
Net transfers also rose to $11.9 billion in June from $10.9 billion, while the net income deficit narrowed to $5.8 billion from $6.8 billion.
On the capital account front, net inflows stood at $9.1 billion in June 2026, compared with an outflow of $1.6 billion in the year-ago month.
Net foreign direct investment stood at $1.3 billion in June, while foreign portfolio investment recorded a net inflow of $2.5 billion.
The overall balance was positive at $2.9 billion in June 2026, against a deficit of $0.4 billion in June 2025.
During the April-June quarter, the merchandise trade deficit widened to $85.7 billion from $68.9 billion, while the services surplus increased to $52.2 billion from $47.9 billion.
Net transfers rose to $41.4 billion during April-June 2026 from $30.9 billion in the year-ago period.
The overall balance during the quarter was negative at $8.1 billion compared with a positive $4.5 billion in April-June 2025, the RBI data showed.

stories.headline: Trump admin accuses over 40 nations including India of helping China evade tariffs - what it means
stories.deck: The White House report classifies more than 40 countries into three separate tiers based on their alleged role in transshipment activities. India has been placed in Tier 1, labelled "Diversified Scale Leaders", alongside Canada, the European Union, Israel, Japan, Mexico, South Korea and Taiwan.
stories.bodyText:
A new US report has alleged that India is among 40 countries that are helping China evade Trump’s tariffs with the help of a shadow trans-shipment network. The White House on August 13, 2026, released a 25-page report titled The Great Transshipment Scam: Rise, Scope, and Costs, alleging that Chinese exporters are routing goods through more than 40 countries to bypass higher US tariffs.
Prepared by the White House Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy under Peter Navarro, the report argues that while the Section 301 tariffs introduced against China in 2018 reduced direct Chinese exports to the United States, they also gave rise to a worldwide transshipment network.
According to the report, Chinese products are being relabelled, repackaged, re-invoiced or subjected to limited processing in countries facing lower US tariff rates before being exported to the United States under a different country of origin. The report describes this system as the “Shadow Transshipment Network.”
To illustrate the scale of the issue, the report cites five separate estimates of annual transshipment or related exposure: $40 billion from Goldman Sachs, $60 billion from the White House Council of Economic Advisers, $75 billion from Exiger, $109 billion from the US Commerce Department and $303 billion from Altana. It also notes that these estimates are based on different methodologies and therefore cannot be directly compared.
India named
The report classifies more than 40 countries into three separate tiers based on their alleged role in transshipment activities. India has been placed in Tier 1, labelled "Diversified Scale Leaders", alongside Canada, the European Union, Israel, Japan, Mexico, South Korea and Taiwan. According to the report, these economies possess large industrial manufacturing bases where alleged transshipment risks are intertwined with legitimate trade flows.
Tier 2, described as "Significant Economic Integration with China", comprises Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Turkey and Vietnam. Tier 3, labelled "Small, Opportunistic Targets", includes Bangladesh, Cambodia, the Philippines, Singapore, Sri Lanka and the UAE.
During a media briefing, senior White House trade adviser Peter Navarro specifically referred to India while cautioning that countries could attempt to circumvent higher US tariffs through transshipment as Washington expands its tariff measures.
"This is about the 40-plus countries that are enabling the transshipping, and as we impose higher tariffs on other countries, India, Vietnam, down the line, they're going to try this transhipment too. Our message is simply that the way to pay less is not to cheat; it is to stop dumping, respect intellectual property, drop your barriers to American goods and move towards reciprocity. Our warning to the lower tariff countries facilitating and enabling the transshipping is this: preferential access to the American market is not a license to launder somebody else's exports," said Navarro.
The report refers to a US Commerce Department estimate that goods worth $67 billion were transshipped through India, Mexico and Vietnam in 2025, resulting in tariff losses of $28 billion. However, it does not specify India's share of that estimate, identify any Indian exporter or provide details of a single fraudulent shipment.
According to the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), the report also singles out India's Pune-Gujarat-Chennai manufacturing corridor for products classified under HS codes 8413-8414, covering pumps and compressors.
However, an analysis by GTRI indicates that India has significant domestic manufacturing capability in these product categories.
During FY2026, India exported liquid pumps worth $1.61 billion worldwide, including shipments worth $414.5 million to the United States, while importing liquid pumps valued at $326.4 million from China. Similarly, India exported air pumps and gas compressors worth $1.48 billion globally, of which $335.4 million went to the US, even as imports from China stood at $1.63 billion.
Given the scale of India's worldwide exports in these sectors, GTRI argues that it is difficult to assume that shipments to the United States merely consist of Chinese products being rerouted through India.
Trump tariff failure?
According to GTRI, the new report is a way of shifting focus away from tariff outcomes of the 
Donald Trump
 administration.
Although US imports from China declined from $525.8 billion in 2017 to $327.5 billion in 2025, America's overall imports continued to rise, increasing from $2.41 trillion to $3.50 trillion over the same period.
“The US therefore replaced many Chinese finished goods with imports from other countries rather than with domestic production. Trump’s tariffs changed the source of imports but failed to reduce America’s overall dependence on imported goods,” says GTRI founder Ajay Srivastava.
China, meanwhile, appears to have adjusted its export strategy. Instead of relying primarily on direct exports of finished goods to the United States, it has increasingly supplied components and intermediate products to manufacturers in countries such as Mexico, Vietnam, India and several European and Asian economies. These inputs are then processed, assembled or incorporated into finished products before being exported to the US, notes GTRI.
“Where such processing results in substantial transformation, these are genuine exports of the manufacturing country and an established feature of global value chains. They cannot be treated as Chinese transshipment merely because they contain Chinese inputs. China has, in effect, responded to US tariffs by strengthening its position as a global supplier of intermediate goods,” GTRI says.
The report also points out that aggregate trade figures do not, by themselves, establish widespread rerouting of Chinese exports. Chinese imports may be used for domestic consumption, genuine manufacturing activity or exports to destinations other than the United States.
GTRI identifies 4 key shortcomings
According to GTRI, the report suffers from four major weaknesses.
First, it broadens the conventional definition of transshipment, which ordinarily refers to cargo being unloaded and reloaded without alteration, to include activities such as assembly, testing, finishing and component integration. In doing so, it conflates genuine manufacturing with origin fraud and risks portraying legitimate production within global supply chains as transshipment without first establishing any violation.
Second, the report relies on trade correlations as evidence. A reduction in direct imports from China accompanied by rising imports from another country does not, by itself, demonstrate that the same goods were simply relabelled and rerouted.
Third, GTRI argues that it is the United States' own country-specific tariff structure that has created the large tariff differentials making evasion financially attractive.
Fourth, although the United States already applies non-preferential rules of origin based on the principle of substantial transformation, the report argues that these rules remain complex, inconsistent and susceptible to misuse, while recommending stricter statutory standards.
What India should do
India should seek evidence and conduct its own verification, says Ajay Srivastava.
GTRI says India should ask the United States to disclose the detailed basis of its allegations, including country-specific, product-level and shipment-level data, as well as India's share of the estimated $67 billion in alleged transshipped goods.
It also recommends that India independently examine exports of pumps and compressors by comparing firm-level imports from China with exports to the United States and verifying the extent of domestic value addition. Such an exercise would help identify any misuse, safeguard compliant exporters and enable India to contest unsubstantiated allegations with credible evidence.

stories.headline: US stock market today: Wall Street drifts near record highs; economic data in focus
stories.deck: The bond market was largely steady after government data showed that consumer spending at US retailers declined from the previous month. The reading caught economists off guard, as they had expected retail sales to post another monthly increase.
stories.bodyText:
US stock market today: Wall Street benchmarks were trading close to their record highs on Friday despite another unexpectedly weak economic indicator, this time showing softer retail spending.
The S&P 500 inched up 0.1%, following the record close it achieved a day earlier. As of 9:35 a.m. Eastern time, the Dow Jones Industrial Average had slipped 27 points, or 0.1%, while the Nasdaq Composite was trading 0.1% higher.
The bond market was largely steady after government data showed that consumer spending at US retailers declined from the previous month. The reading caught economists off guard, as they had expected retail sales to post another monthly increase, according to an AP report.
Stocks in focus
Among individual stocks on Wall Street, Reddit surged 14.7% after it was announced that the company would be added to the S&P 500 index on Tuesday. Inclusion in the benchmark typically attracts buying from index funds and institutional investors that either replicate the index or use it as a performance benchmark.
Applied Materials declined 4% despite reporting quarterly revenue and profit that exceeded analysts' expectations. 
The semiconductor equipment maker said strong global demand for artificial intelligence technologies helped it deliver another record quarter. CEO Gary Dickerson credited the growing appetite for AI as a key driver of the company's performance.
However, the stock came under pressure after having more than doubled in value this year, leaving investor expectations exceptionally high.
The broader AI sector has remained volatile in recent months amid concerns that share prices had risen too quickly on enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence and that the rapid pace of revenue growth may not be sustainable.
What softer retail sales mean
From the market's perspective, weaker consumer spending could help ease inflationary pressures. Although inflation remains well above desired levels, data released earlier in the week indicated that the pace of price increases has begun to moderate.
If that trend continues, the Federal Reserve may choose to delay raising interest rates. While higher borrowing costs are an effective tool to curb inflation, they also restrain economic activity by making loans more expensive for households and businesses.
However, the softer retail sales figures, coupled with last week's unexpectedly weak employment report, have also fuelled fears that the US economy may be losing momentum.
Even so, some market participants urged caution in interpreting the retail sales data. 
Short-term Treasury yields edged lower after the retail sales report, indicating that traders now see a reduced likelihood of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates at its September policy meeting.
The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield, which is more sensitive to long-term expectations for inflation and economic growth, edged higher to 4.65% from 4.63% at Thursday's close.
Oil prices stable
In the commodities market, oil prices were relatively stable after experiencing sharp swings in recent weeks, as markets continued to react to changing expectations over when the conflict involving Iran might ease sufficiently to allow crude shipments from the Middle East to resume normal global flows.
Brent crude slipped 0.2% to $86.92 a barrel.
Overseas equity markets ended with mixed performances across Europe and Asia.
In the UK, London's FTSE 100 eased 0.1% after Nigel Farage won back the parliamentary seat he had vacated a month earlier, defeating the novelty candidate Count Binface, who campaigned wearing a trash can.
South Korea's Kospi was once again among the world's best-performing major indices, advancing 2.4% for its third consecutive session with gains of at least that magnitude. The Seoul market has been at the centre of the global volatility in AI-related stocks because of the dominant influence of technology giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

briefs.headline: India's green bonds find footing as stable 'greenium' underscores investor appetite
briefs.deck: New Delhi sold 50 billion rupees ($524 ⁠million) of 30-year sovereign green bonds, at a so-called greenium of four basis points on Friday, leading to an average premium of four bps ‌in the fiscal half-year, the highest since such sales began in the second half of fiscal 2023
briefs.bodyText:
A persistent premium over comparable government debt, alongside strong and steady demand from insurance companies , has convinced market participants that a larger supply of Indian sovereign green bonds can be absorbed in the second half of the fiscal year.
New Delhi sold 50 billion rupees ($524 million) of 30-year sovereign green bonds, at a so-called greenium of four basis points on Friday, leading to an average premium of four bps in the fiscal half-year, the highest since such sales began in the second half of fiscal 2023.
A greenium is the lower yield investors are willing to accept for bonds that finance environmentally sustainable projects.
“Green bonds are eligible for classification under the infrastructure category, which provides an added benefit for insurance companies from an asset allocation and regulatory perspective,” said Shobit Gupta, chief investment officer, Generali Central Life Insurance.
“The existing demand-supply dynamics have resulted in a noticeable greenium, with green bonds trading richer than comparable conventional government securities,” he said.
Including the latest issuance, India now has sovereign green bonds worth 877 billion rupees or $9.2 billion outstanding. Notes with 30-year maturities are the most issued, crossing the 500 billion rupee mark.
Strong demand has led to calls by market participants for some increase in the supply of such papers, as insurers manage a growing corpus and find a lack of sufficient substitutes.
“We believe the market is well positioned to absorb a higher supply of green bonds in the second half of FY27, particularly if the issuance is concentrated in the longer part of the curve,” said Sachin Bajaj, chief investment officer at Axis Max Life Insurance.
“Demand for these bonds continues to be supported by insurers’ ALM requirements.”
After starting with five-year and 10-year green bonds in January 2023, New Delhi had to cancel or cut the size of a few issuances, before ultimately selling these papers at yields above those ofcomparable government bonds.
However, the greenium returned with the government sticking to issuing 30-year green bonds in the last 18 months.
“Long green bond issuance has remained consistent over the past three fiscal years, adequately matching current investor demand,” Rahul Bhuskute, CIO at Bharti AXA Life Insurance said.

briefs.headline: Coal demand to touch 1.6 billion tonnes by 2030; need transparent, market-driven pricing: Official
briefs.deck: "Coal demand is projected to rise further to an estimated 1.6 billion tonnes by 2030," Dutt said, adding that we are at an "inflection point" where we are shifting from a scarcity scenario to one of surplus
briefs.bodyText:
India's coal demand is likely to touch 1.6 billion tonnes per annum by 2030, a top government official said on Friday (August 14, 2026), underlining the need for transparent and market-driven pricing for the commodity.
Speaking at the Global Commodities Conclave Mumbai, Union Coal Secretary Vikram Dev Dutt said that the setting up of the 'coal exchange', a government-established platform designed to work as an independent marketplace, will be of help.
He said in each of the last two fiscal years, domestic coal production has crossed 1 billion metric tonnes and the demand is continuing to grow as the commodity is a mainstay of energy needs.
"Coal demand is projected to rise further to an estimated 1.6 billion tonnes by 2030," Dutt said, adding that we are at an "inflexion point" where we are shifting from a scarcity scenario to one of surplus.
Such a shift underscores the need for "more efficient, transparent and market driven mechanisms for coal trade", he said, pointing out that till now the state-run Coal India has enjoyed a virtual "monopoly".
"While this model did serve its purpose for the time that it was designed, it does not fully reflect the competitive, transparent and efficient price discovery that a market of India's scale and India's maturity deserves," he added.
The coal exchanges will provide commercial and captive miners ready and transparent access to a wider market, wherein buyers and sellers can bid simultaneously enabling efficient, competitive, and market-driven price discovery, he said.
The government plans to operationalise the coal exchange concept in "the months ahead", he said, without sharing affirm timeline.
The exchange will function as a central counterparty for clearing and settlement thereby improving risk management for both buyers and seller, he said, adding that it can also help lay the foundation for a derivatives market for coal over a period of time.
Coal exchange is a reform that reflects the government's commitment to enable and enhance ease of doing business, promote transparency and build a modern self-reliant energy ecosystem, Dutt said, hoping that it will strengthen India's energy security, support industrial growth and contribute meaningfully to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

briefs.headline: Ashok Leyland posts record Q1 earnings but higher costs squeeze margins
briefs.deck: Commercial vehicle maker flags commodity cost pressures, maintains ₹1,000-crore investment plan and says AI is deployed to improve productivity and not replace workforce
briefs.bodyText:
Ashok Leyland reported record revenue and profit for the June-ended quarter with revenue from operations rising 10% year-on-year to ₹9,634 crore and net profit climbing 3% to ₹609 crore.
However, higher commodity costs weighed on profitability, pulling the EBITDA margin down to 10.1% from 11.1% a year earlier despite record first-quarter commercial vehicle sales.
On a consolidated basis, which includes the group’s financial services businesses, revenue from operations rose about 12% year-on-year to ₹13,070 crore,profit before tax climbed 7% to ₹950 crore and profit after tax rose about 2% to ₹668 crore.
Chairman Dheeraj Hinduja, in a statement said, demand across key segments remained robust and that government initiatives such as Parivartan would accelerate fleet modernisation while strengthening the long-term growth prospects of the commercial vehicle industry.
The company reported its “highest-ever first-quarter” commercial vehicle sales of 48,763 units, led by strong growth in the light commercial vehicle segment. Medium and heavy truck sales also grew during the quarter, although bus sales were affected by state elections in key markets and the company’s decision to avoid unprofitable tenders, management said during the post-earnings briefing.
Exports declined to 2,461 units from 3,011 units due to disruptions caused by the conflict in West Asia. The company said overseas volumes have started recovering and expects international operations to perform better than last year.
The company said it plans to spend around ₹1,000 crore on capital expenditure in FY27, mainly on new product and technology development, while ruling out any immediate capacity expansion.
It also said Switch Mobility India, its electric bus business, is now financially independent. The Chennai-based auto major also proposed an investment of up to £25 million (around ₹325 crore) in Optare Plc, the U.K.-based holding company for the group’s electric mobility businesses, and said it will be used to repay loans and meet business requirements.
On the workforce front, management said Ashok Leyland employed about 30,000 people on its standalone rolls. Responding to questions on Artificial Intelligence (AI), the company said AI is being deployed across manufacturing, sales and after-sales operations to improve productivity rather than reduce headcount.
“Our first goal from deployment of AI is to increase our capability and effectiveness rather than reduce the headcount,” the company said, adding that AI tools are being used to strengthen workshop diagnostics, improve sales effectiveness and provide customers with greater transparency on vehicle health, repair costs and service processes.

briefs.headline: India-focused funds see moderate outflows, ETFs cushion impact
briefs.deck: Foreign portfolio investors’ (FPIs) pullback has resulted in net outflows of ₹2.4 lakh crore as of August 14
briefs.bodyText:
Redemptions from India-focused funds managed by foreign investors, who are drawn to the country’s growth story, moderated in July 2026, with inflows into exchange traded funds (ETFs) cushioning the overall outflows, according to a research note.
“India continues to show gradual improvement in the pace of foreign selling, although the trend remains negative. The moderation over recent weeks is being led by some inflows into India-focused ETFs, while long-only funds remain persistent sellers, a trend that has continued since Jul’25 and accelerated in CY26,” observed Sunil Jain, Vice President at Elara Capital.
India focussed funds started redeeming their investments in India when the net inflow was little less than $20 billion in July 2025 and has continued for a year now. As of July 2026, the foreign funds are now at levels less than $9 billion.
Nearly “65% of the cumulative inflows received by India-focused long-only funds during 2023–24 have now been withdrawn. Some support is beginning to emerge from U.S.-domiciled ETFs, while Japan and Luxembourg remain the biggest sources of pressure, having already withdrawn roughly 50–60% of the capital they invested during 2022–24,” the report said. “While the moderation in the pace of redemptions is encouraging, a sustained reversal in flows is still awaited.”
Foreign portfolio investors’ (FPIs) pullback has resulted in net outflows of ₹2.4 lakh crore as of August 14. The sustained selling has weighed on the rupee and tempered market sentiment. Year-to-date, the Nifty has declined nearly 6%. Domestic investors, including mutual funds and institutional investors, however, have continued to provide support to the market.

briefs.headline: SRTT ban may delay Tata selection committee formation
briefs.deck: As per the Articles of Association of Tata Sons, both Sir Dorab Tata Trust (SDTT) and SRTT have to jointly nominate three members to the five-member selection committee.
briefs.bodyText:
The formation of the selection committee by Tata Trusts to choose the next chairman is likely to be delayed due to restrictions imposed by the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner on Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), which has been barred from convening any meeting or passing any resolution until the dispute over its board composition is decided. The next hearing in the matter is scheduled for September 8, 2026.
As per the Articles of Association (AoA) of Tata Sons, both Sir Dorab Tata Trust (SDTT) and SRTT have to jointly nominate three members to the five-member selection committee. One member will be from Tata Sons and one external member.
Since SRTT is under a regulatory ban, it cannot participate in the selection process for the time being, said analysts. And so the entire selection process will not move forward as desired, they added.
While SRTT owns 23.5% of Tata Sons, SDTT has 27.9%.
A day after N Chandrasekaran, the Chairman of Tata Sons announced his decision not to go for the third term, SDTT passed a resolution to initiate the setting up of a selection committee as soon as possible in accordance with the AoA of Tata Sons, for the purpose of recommending a person for appointment as the new chairman of the Board of Directors. This has been interpreted as a move by SDTT to initiate the process though a decision on SRTT would come later.
Since Mr Chandrasekaran will continue as Chairman till February, 2027, there is time available to finalise the names of the selection committee..
It is believed that Maharashtra Charity Commissioner’s office maybe moved to allow SRTT to convene a meeting and pass a resolution in this matter, which is a procedural one needing urgent intervention rather than approving any budget and having any financial dealing..
According to people familiar with the development, the Tata Trusts may move the court to deal with this extraordinary situation.
