briefs.headline: CAG finds 89% of audited railway stations deficient in basic amenities
briefs.deck: Of 512 stations audited, 458 stations were deficient in one or more minimum essential amenities, including fans, water coolers, drinking water taps, urinals, seating arrangements, platform shelters, latrines and clocks
briefs.bodyText:
An audit of passenger amenities and sanitation by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India has revealed persistent and widespread deficiencies across Indian Railways.
A joint team of CAG and railway officials conducted an audit of 512 stations, of which 458 stations (nearly 89%) were deficient in one or more minimum essential amenities, including fans (42%), water coolers (40%), drinking water taps (27%), urinals (22%), seating arrangements (15%), platform shelters (13%), latrines (12%) and clocks (12%). “Only 54 stations (11%) had no shortfalls,” the report noted.
Of the 512 stations audited, 325 were non-Amrit Bharat stations. The Amrit Bharat Station Scheme is an ongoing initiative of the Railway Ministry, launched in 2022, to modernise over 1,300 railway stations across the country.
The CAG audited non-suburban stations handling long-distance passenger traffic of at least 150 km. The sample sizes were drawn from 5,908 stations across 16 railway zones running 7,424 passenger trains daily and serving 292.4 crore passengers as of 2023-24.
Shortfalls in seating arrangements, sanitary facilities (urinals and latrines), dustbins, and electronic train indicator boards were observed at select stations. This included major terminals categorised as NSG-1 stations (where earnings exceed ₹500 crore and/or outward passengers exceed 20 million annually) such as Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Howrah, Sealdah, New Delhi and Mumbai Central, indicating gaps in the maintenance and monitoring of essential facilities.
Other stations where shortfalls were observed include Naihati, Gaya, Bhagalpur, Bhopal and Rajkot. Interestingly, the CAG pointed out these shortfalls in three previous audits in 2007, 2013 and 2016.
“Persistent shortfalls in amenities were attributable to inadequate monitoring of implementation of the Railway Board Circular dated April 9, 2018, absence of time-bound action plans, weak oversight of fund utilisation under Plan Head and inconsistent prioritisation of works at zonal level,” the report stated.
In September 2012, the Railway Board had instructed that platform shelters should cover the area where general second-class coaches stop. However, the audit noticed that this was not ensured at 379 stations. “Thus, passengers remained exposed to vagaries of weather,” the report noted.
“All stations must be provided with clocks. However, in 60 stations no clock was provided. Also, dustbins were not provided as per norms at 149 stations,” the report stated.
A review of 395 passenger amenity works across 325 non-Amrit Bharat stations showed that 59% of works were delayed (from one to over four years) and only 41% were completed within stipulated timelines, thus depriving passengers of timely access to essential facilities.
The CAG has observed that there is a risk that lower-priority works may be undertaken under the guise of redevelopment in the Railways, while long-pending compliance with mandatory norms continues to be compromised or diluted.
The CAG report stated that deficiencies in monitoring, enforcement and accountability at all levels diluted the objective of ensuring minimum essential passenger amenities and sanitation standards at stations, despite the availability of means and resources to address the issues.
Systemic failure
The report noted the persistent underutilisation of budget grants for providing passenger amenities, ranging between 36% and 44% during 2019-20 to 2023-24, even in non-COVID years, revealing deficiencies in planning and execution rather than financial constraints. Funds are allocated annually to each zonal railway for passenger amenity works.
While the fund allocation largely remained stable at ₹3,207 crore (2019-20), ₹3,875 crore (2020-21), ₹3,414 crore (2021-22) and ₹3,351 crore (2022-23), it shot up to ₹14,072 crore in 2023-24. The CAG report noted a significant year-on-year underutilisation of budget grants — ₹1,403 crore (44%), ₹1,499 crore (39%), ₹1,423 crore (42%), ₹1,198 crore (36%) and ₹5,956 crore (42%) during the five-year period.
Meanwhile, passenger earnings increased from ₹42,190 crore in 2014-15 to ₹70,693 crore in 2023-24. Also, the number of originating non-suburban passengers declined from 3,719 million in 2014-15 to 2,924 million in 2023-24, largely attributable to COVID.
A further analysis of Passenger Amenities Management System (PAMS) data from February 2025 confirmed that deficiencies persisted across all station categories and zones, signalling systemic gaps rather than isolated cases.
The data analysis of 5,908 stations revealed shortages of latrines in 214 stations, urinals in 91 stations, water taps in 1,440 stations and public address systems in 1,983 stations.
Contrary to Railway Board instructions, the report stated that no time-bound action plans were prepared to bridge gaps in recommended and desirable amenities.
Inadequate facilities
The report also noted that accessibility infrastructure for Divyangjans (persons with disabilities) was inadequate and non-compliant, with substantial deficiencies in accessibility infrastructure, information systems, toilets, ramps, tactile pathways, lifts and announcements. For example, at Madurai Junction (SR), the tactile pathway was incorrectly laid instead of at the prescribed distance of 1,800 mm from the platform edge.
Out of 374 Divyangjans interviewed, 131 (35%) reported that the amenities were inadequate. The deficiencies cited included non-functional or closed toilets without information on key availability, absence of low-height drinking water facilities, parking, non-slippery pathways, lifts, portable ramps and low-height ticket counters, inconvenient platform heights, uncooperative battery car services, and lack of announcements regarding Divyangjans coach positions.
Also, availability of first-aid medical care for passengers was inadequate.
The CAG report noted that there were deficiencies in the implementation of station cleaning contracts. “Non-compliance to Standard Bid Document (SBD) by the zones and non-uniformity in adoption of SBD across the divisions were noticed,” the report said.
Also, inefficiency of the zonal railways led to non-utilisation of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds.
For instance, in Southern Railway, during 2020–2023, 187 pre-fabricated toilets were installed at a cost of ₹0.25 crore per unit. Out of these, 79 toilets remained non-operational due to the absence of service providers for operation and maintenance. Consequently, CSR fund investment of ₹19.75 crore by M/s Neyveli Lignite Corporation remained unutilised as of February 2025, the CAG report noted.
Similarly, in Eastern Railway, a bio-toilet complex installed at Plassey station in December 2022 remained non-functional due to non-availability of water and electricity. The audit further observed that the station authorities did not escalate the issue to the divisional level for arranging water and electricity supply as of March 2025.
In East Coast Railway, during 2021–2024, 92 pre-fabricated toilet blocks were provided at a cost of ₹0.25 crore per unit. Of these, 62 toilet blocks remained non-operational due to factors such as non-deployment of contractual staff, availability of existing Pay & Use toilets at stations, and delays in finalisation of bids through e-auction. As a result, CSR fund investment of ₹15.50 crore by M/s Mahanadi Coalfields Limited remained unutilised as of March 2025, the CAG report noted.
The CAG report proposed that the Railways prepare and deploy station-wise, time-bound action plans to address amenity concerns, including effectively implementing accessibility provisions for Divyangjans and strengthening sanitation and garbage management measures.
The CAG has also recommended that the Railways should ensure regular functioning of all consultative committees and Service Improvement Groups with effective documentation, supervision and follow-up on deficiencies.
The Railways should also strengthen passenger-centric monitoring by improving enforcement of anti-littering rules, enhancing grievance redressal and publicity of complaint registers to achieve tangible improvements at stations, the CAG report noted.

briefs.headline: States turn to solar subsidies to offset losses from subsidised power
briefs.deck: The approach primarily entails that states’ additional subsidy on subsidising power is streamed as capital expenditure for financing rooftop solar installation, officials stated.
briefs.bodyText:
To reduce the revenue losses incurred from subsidising electricity, several states, including Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Bihar, are providing financial assistance to households that cannot afford rooftop solar installations., J.V.N. Subramanyam, Joint Secretary at the Union New and Renewable Ministry told The Hindu.
The ₹75,000 crore Pradhan Mantri – Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojna, expects to install rooftop solar (RTS) in one crore households by March 2027. Households are incentivised to do so by offering subsidised installations, bank loans as well as easing the multiple steps the process usually involves.
The scheme currently allots 300 units of “free” power a month to those who install. It emerged, however, that there were households, who had no incentive to install RTS, because they were already getting free power under state schemes.
Rather than continue bearing the recurring costs of providing free daytime electricity, some states are opting, under the Utility-Led Aggregation Model (ULA), to incur a one-time capital expenditure to install RTS.“The approach herein (that is, with the utility-linked aggregation model) entails that additional subsidy [from the states] is modulated as a one-time capital expenditure for installing rooftop solar [setup],” he said.
Currently only those households with a suitable rooftop and are connected to the grid can avail RTS. The scheme doesn’t subsidise storage batteries.
As on August 13, 52 lakh households have installed Surya Ghar RTS. Mr. Subramanyam said that about 2 lakh installations of the stipulated target of 30 lakh installations under the ULA component of the ministry’s PM Surya Ghar have been completed in the ongoing phase.
“Installations have picked up in the last three-four months. There is an uptick and interest from several states including Bihar, Jammu and Kashmir and Rajasthan.,” he said.
A survey by the think tank, Council on Energy Environment and Water (CEEW) in June on adoption patterns under Surya Ghar said that to reach the 10 million mark by March 2027, India needs to sustain its current momentum to solarise 0.6 million households per month between June 2026 to March 2027. “At the same time, there can be an increased effort to diversify the adoption beyond the five states-Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Kerala, accounting for more than 71 % of national installed capacity,” the report noted.
The survey found that 73% of households that perceive RTS as expensive were unaware of available financing options. Among those who were willing to consider the model, households with low electricity consumption were reportedly the most reluctant to contribute to the upfront cost of installing RTS.
Addressing the affordability barriers faced by households that are aware of RTS but are not interested in adopting it, through suitable financing options, could unlock a theoretical convertible demand of 22.7 GW, according to the report .

stories.headline: Ryanair mocks Argentina after World Cup winner Rodri spotted on ultra-low-budget flight
stories.deck: Ryanair joined the viral reaction to Rodri’s budget flight from Madrid to Liverpool with a cheeky message aimed at Argentina. The airline tagged the Argentina national team while declaring, “We only fly winners,” referencing Spain’s World Cup triumph and Rodri’s Golden Ball. The post quickly went viral, adding football rivalry to the Manchester City star’s unlikely journey home.
stories.bodyText:
Ryanair has joined the growing social-media frenzy around Rodri's unlikely journey home, turning the Manchester City midfielder's viral economy-flight appearance into an opportunity for some football banter. After the Spain international was photographed boarding one of its flights from Madrid to Liverpool, the airline aimed its latest joke at Argentina with a pointed message about who qualifies as a “winner”.
Ryanair gets involved in the Rodri frenzy
The viral moment began when Rodri was spotted waiting to board a Ryanair flight, wearing a baseball cap and sunglasses in an apparent attempt to keep a low profile.
His personalised suitcase, carrying his name, Spain's flag and his squad number, quickly gave him away, and photographs of the 2024 Ballon d'Or winner travelling on a budget airline spread across social media.
Ryanair wasted little time joining the conversation.
The airline's official social-media account tagged the Argentina national team and posted the line: “We only fly winners.”
The remark was a deliberately cheeky reference to Rodri's recent international success with Spain and the rivalry between the two football nations.
The joke was aimed at Argentina's recent misfortunes
Rodri's journey had already attracted attention because of the contrast between his status and his choice of transport. The 30-year-old is one of the most decorated midfielders in the game, yet he was photographed standing in an ordinary airport queue rather than travelling privately.
Ryanair's response shifted the story from admiration for Rodri's low-key approach towards football banter.
The post quickly generated significant engagement online, with hundreds of thousands of interactions reported within hours as supporters reacted to the airline's attempt to turn a viral photograph into a piece of topical marketing.
For Rodri, the attention comes after a remarkable summer with Spain. He was part of the World Cup-winning side and received the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player, adding another major individual honour to the Ballon d'Or he won in 2024.

stories.headline: Rodri stuns passengers on ultra-budget Ryanair flight to Liverpool after World Cup glory
stories.deck: World Cup Golden Ball winner Rodri stunned fellow passengers by boarding a budget Ryanair flight from Madrid to Liverpool. The Manchester City star attempted to stay unnoticed under a cap and sunglasses, but his personalised suitcase gave him away. Despite his superstar status, Rodri remained approachable, even accepting a World Cup sticker from a travelling family before heading back to England.
stories.bodyText:
Rodri has spent the past year at the very top of world football, but the Manchester City midfielder offered a rather different image of himself while making his way back to England. The 30-year-old Spain international was spotted queuing for a budget Ryanair flight from Madrid to Liverpool, leaving fellow passengers stunned as they realised who was standing among them.
The midfielder, who was crowned the 2026 World Cup's Golden Ball winner after helping Spain lift the trophy, appeared to make little effort to draw attention to himself.
Rodri tried to keep a low profile
Rodri was wearing a baseball cap pulled down over his forehead and dark sunglasses while waiting at the departure gate in Madrid.
The disguise was not particularly effective.
His personalised mini suitcase gave away his identity, with the luggage carrying his name, the Spanish national team flag and his squad number. Once passengers recognised him, photographs and videos of the midfielder quickly began circulating online.
The sight of one of football's most decorated players waiting for a low-cost commercial flight immediately caught attention, particularly because elite footballers of Rodri's standing routinely have access to private aviation.
One social media user joked: “Guys... why is Rodri getting on our Ryanair flight?”
Another called it “truly iconic stuff from Rodri flying Ryanair”, while another imagined the reaction of passengers discovering the Manchester City star in their queue: “Imagine boarding your Ryanair flight and seeing Rodri standing in the same queue as you!”
Fans were even more impressed by what happened next
The low-key journey did not stop at Rodri simply choosing a budget airline.
Eyewitnesses said the midfielder remained relaxed and approachable despite the attention around him. One travelling family reportedly handed him a World Cup sticker they had found in their luggage, which Rodri accepted before exchanging a fist-bump with the children.
The episode quickly became another reason for supporters to praise his understated approach away from the pitch.
That reaction was particularly striking given Rodri's status. He won the Ballon d'Or in 2024, having helped Manchester City win the Premier League and Spain claim Euro 2024, and was later named the best player of the 2026 World Cup.
His decision to travel alongside ordinary passengers nevertheless made him look considerably more like a regular traveller than one of football's biggest stars.
Rodri is heading back to Manchester City
The flight also comes as Rodri prepares to return to club duties following Spain's World Cup triumph.
He was due back at Manchester City's Etihad Campus, although it remained unclear whether he would immediately resume training. The midfielder is also set to miss Sunday's Community Shield.
There is an additional reason for caution around his return. Rodri underwent minor back surgery last month after experiencing what was described as “discomfort”, and no definitive timeline had been established for his return to first-team football.
That uncertainty comes alongside continued speculation over his future, with Barcelona reportedly maintaining interest in bringing the Spain international back to La Liga.
For now, however, Rodri's journey from Madrid to Liverpool suggests his immediate focus is on getting back to England and preparing for the new season with City. And rather than arriving in a private jet, he did it in a way that left fellow Ryanair passengers wondering if they had somehow ended up sharing a flight with one of the most recognisable midfielders in the world.

stories.headline: Jimmy Rimmer, European Cup winner with Man United and Aston Villa, dies at age 78
stories.deck: Two-time European Cup-winning goalkeeper Jimmy Rimmer has died at age 78; he was at United from 1965-74 and then had three years at Arsenal before playing for Villa from 1977-83
stories.bodyText:
Jimmy Rimmer, a goalkeeper who won the European Cup with English teams Manchester United and Aston Villa 14 years apart, has died. He was 78.
Villa announced the death of Rimmer on Friday without giving any more details. The club described him as “one of the finest goalkeepers of his generation, and arguably one of the unluckiest when it came to big occasions.”
Rimmer collected a European Cup winner's medal with United in 1968 after being on the bench, as the backup to Alex Stepney, for its 4-1 win over Benfica in the final at Wembley Stadium.
In the 1982 final, Rimmer started for Villa in a 1-0 win over Bayern Munich in Rotterdam, Netherlands, but came off with a neck injury after nine minutes and was in tears in the locker room. He was able to join the post-match celebrations, though, after Peter Withe’s winner.
Rimmer started all nine of Villa matches in the competition that season, after being an ever-present in its English league title-winning campaign the previous season.
He was at United from 1965-74 and then had three years at Arsenal before playing for Villa from 1977-83.
Rimmer played once for England — a friendly against Italy in 1976.
In a post on X, United said it was “deeply saddened” by Rimmer's death, adding: “Our thoughts are with Jimmy’s loved ones at this difficult time.”

stories.headline: Jemimah Rodrigues ruled out of Asia Cup and Asian Games due to hamstring injury
stories.deck: The BCCI said in a statement that the 25-year-old Rodrigues has been assessed by the medical team with a high-grade tear
stories.bodyText:
India women's team batter Jemimah Rodrigues was on Friday ruled out of the upcoming Asia Cup and Asian Games due to a hamstring injury she sustained earlier this month while playing in The Hundred tournament in England.
The BCCI said in a statement that the 25-year-old Rodrigues has been assessed by the medical team with a high-grade tear.
The Women's Selection Committee has named Pratika Rawal as Rodrigues' replacement for the Asia Cup to be played in Dubai from August 28 to September 13.
"Jemimah Rodrigues sustained a right hamstring injury on 3rd August while playing in The Hundred in England. The BCCI Medical Team clinically assessed her at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, and the assessment confirmed a high-grade tear," the Board said.
"Consequently, she has been ruled out of the upcoming ACC Women’s Asia Cup in the UAE and the Asian Games in Japan." The Asian Games will be held in Aichi-Nagoya in Japan from September 19 to October 4.
India's updated Asia Cup squad: Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Smriti Mandhana (VC), Shafali Verma, Bharti Fulmali, Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh (WK), G. Kamalini (WK), Arundhati Reddy, Prema Rawat, Radha Yadav, Sree Charani, Renuka Thakur, Nandni Sharma, Kranti Gaud, Pratika Rawal.

briefs.headline: Praggnanandhaa bounces back; crushes Van Foreest
briefs.deck: The victory helped Praggnanandhaa reach 2.5 points from four games in the 10-player-nine-round event
briefs.bodyText:
Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa bounced back from his previous loss to crush Dutchman Jorden Van Foreest in the fourth round for a share of the second spot at the Sinquefield Cup here.
The victory helped Praggnanandhaa reach 2.5 points from four games in the 10-player-nine-round event.
Having lost the previous round against Vincent Keymer of Germany, this comeback is surely going to boost his chances for the podium to qualify for the finale of the Grand Chess tour.
Incidentally, this was the lone decisive game of the day as the remaining four ended in draws leaving Wesley So of United States still in lead on three points after his draw with compatriot Levon Aronian.
In the other all-American clash, Fabiano Caruana was held to a draw by Sevian Samuel while Anish Giri drew with world championship contender Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan.
In the other game of the day, Maxime Vachier-Lagrave signed peace with Vincent Keymer of Germany leaving the field wide open in this USD 4,75,000 prize money tournament.
Praggnanandhaa yet again reclaimed the tag of hero-of-the-day with his simple yet effective tactical display right from the word go. It was a King pawn game that the Indian decided to keep close and his strike came very early as by move 12 itself, he was on the path to victory.
Van Foreest did not have a clue as he lost his queen for a rook and a minor piece. As has been the case study before, when it comes to technique there are very few who can match Praggnanandhaa and he did not disappoint his fans.
With five rounds still to be played and Wesley So in command, Praggnanandhaa, Vachier-Lagrave and Aronian are in close pursuit of the leader half a point behind while the wolf-pack having Caruana, Keymer and Samules is not far away on two points each.
Anish Giri and Sindarov share the eighth spot with 1.5 points in their kitty while Van Foreest is still in the cellar with just a half point thus far.

briefs.headline: WTA Chennai Open from November 2 to 8
briefs.deck: TNTA president Vijay Amritraj said that almost all the corporates that had supported the tournament in the past had come forward again to back the event in its third year
briefs.bodyText:
Having received the initial support of ₹10 crore from the Government of Tamil Nadu recently for hosting the WTA 250 Chennai Open international women’s tennis championship to be held here from November 2 to 8, the Tamil Nadu Tennis Association (TNTA) is confident of securing the remaining sponsorship for the tournament.
TNTA president Vijay Amritraj said at a press conference here on Friday that almost all the corporates that had supported the tournament in the past had come forward again to back the event in its third year.
“I am proud to announce the fact that pretty much most of the sponsors that we’ve had alongside the Government of Tamil Nadu for the last couple of years have also given us the support to come back,” said the 72-year-old while profusely thanking the State’s Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for supporting tennis.
The Chennai Open, will have, for the first time, an electronic line calling technology in all the courts—Centre Court and the three outside courts. Last year, Hawk Eye was employed only at the Centre Court. Amritraj said talks are on to get “two to four world’s top-50 players this time.”
Sandeep Nanduri, Secretary, Youth Welfare and Sports Development Department, Government of Tamil Nadu, assured complete support to TNTA in hosting a successful tournament. “We are very happy that the event is being jointly organised with TNTA and whatever support is required, our SDAT-Nungambakkam stadium will be geared up,” he said. Nanduri insisted that Government is trying to get the men’s ATP 250 event back to the State. “.....We are also aiming to bring the ATP 250 event [back] also to Tamil Nadu. I am sure TNTA will support that dream of our department,” he said.

briefs.headline: Family absent from wedding: Presenter claims Ronaldo kin had no notice
briefs.deck: Cristiano Ronaldo’s wedding secrecy has taken another twist after Portuguese presenter Cristina Ferreira claimed his family may have learned about the ceremony just “30 seconds beforehand.” Ronaldo’s mother and siblings were absent when he married Georgina Rodríguez in Cascais on August 11. However, Ferreira’s comments remain unconfirmed, with no indication from Ronaldo or his family that they…
briefs.bodyText:
Cristiano Ronaldo’s decision to keep his wedding to Georgina Rodríguez almost entirely private has raised another question after a Portuguese television presenter claimed that even members of his immediate family may have received virtually no notice that the ceremony was taking place.
The claim comes after the couple’s marriage certificate revealed that Ronaldo’s mother, Dolores Aveiro, and his siblings Hugo, Elma and Katia were not present when he and Rodríguez married at their Cascais home on August 11. Only four witnesses and the couple’s five children attended the intimate civil ceremony.
‘30 seconds beforehand’
The extraordinary claim was made by Portuguese presenter Cristina Ferreira on the TVI programme Dois às 10 while discussing the absence of Ronaldo’s family from the ceremony, according to 
The Sun.
“It will cause a lot of problems because the family wasn’t present,” Ferreira said. She then suggested that they may not even have known the wedding was happening until moments before it began.
“And they shouldn’t even have known,” she said. “Or if they did know, it was 30 seconds beforehand.”
Ferreira’s comments are a claim rather than confirmation from Ronaldo or his family, and her co-host Cláudio Ramos urged caution about drawing conclusions from what was visible publicly.
“I really hope that what we said here, which had to do with the impressions we get from what exists on social media, did not actually cause sadness in the family, that things were not as they apparently seem,” Ramos said.
Ronaldo’s mother was not at the ceremony
The claim comes after Jornal de Notícias obtained and published the couple’s marriage certificate, providing the first detailed account of who was present.
The document names Miguel Paixão, Ronaldo’s longtime friend, Ivana Rodríguez, Georgina’s sister, and Spanish jeweller José Rodríguez Sangil and his wife Mónica González Martínez as the four witnesses.
Ronaldo’s mother and three siblings were not among them.
That absence is particularly notable because Dolores publicly appeared to support the marriage after Ronaldo and Rodríguez announced it. She responded to her son’s Instagram post showing their wedding rings with a heart emoji.
There is therefore no public indication from Dolores herself that she objected to the marriage, while the presenter’s comments have introduced a different possibility: that the ceremony was kept so tightly controlled that even Ronaldo’s family may have been informed only at the last moment.
The wedding was kept deliberately small
Ronaldo and Rodríguez married at 1.30pm on August 11 at their mansion in the exclusive Quinta da Marinha area of Cascais, with a registrar travelling from Porto to officiate.
The couple had previously given the public almost no reliable information about their plans. Reports had even sent hundreds of fans and journalists to Funchal Cathedral in Madeira after it was wrongly claimed that Ronaldo would marry there.
Instead, the couple married privately in Cascais and announced the news only afterwards, posting photographs of their wedding rings with the caption “C❤️G.”

briefs.headline: Tamil Nadu Premier League | Dragons breathe fire with a big win over Spartans
briefs.bodyText:
When persistent rain and a delayed start kept Spartans waiting, little would they have known what was about to hit them. However, once the skies cleared and the match began, there was nowhere to hide.
Dindigul Dragons captain B. Indrajith (73, 25b, 3x4, 8x6) led a breathtaking assault to hand the Spartans an 81-run thrashing in a 15-over-a-side Tamil Nadu Premier League clash at the NPR College ground here on Friday.
The Dragons’ innings began in breathless fashion as openers Shivam Singh (38) and V.K. Vineeth (45) tore into the bowling, racing to 70 in only four overs. Vineeth’s run-out briefly offered the Salem Spartans some respite before debutant E. Krish departed for a golden duck, but the Salem outfit was under the pump soon after. Vimal Khumar (35, 17b, 1x4, 3x6) and Indrajith took over and turned the heat on the Spartans’ bowlers, putting on 62 off just 24 balls for the fourth wicket.
Boundaries flowed with such regularity that the opposition looked clueless. Even Vimal’s dismissal did little to stem the flow of runs.
Indrajith, joined by Hunny Saini (29, 10b, 2x4, 3x6), took the attack apart in the 13th over bowled by M. Poiyamozhi, plundering 32 runs with four maximums and a four.
The onslaught continued in the following over against Uday Kumar, with the pair clearing the ropes four more times, as Dragons finished with 239 for six. The mammoth chase was headed in only one direction, and Dragons made sure the Spartans were never in with a shout.
In the second match, Mokit Hariharan’s maiden century (108, 50b, 4x4, 10x6) and a record-breaking 169-run opening stand with Chepauk Super Gillies captain N. Jagadeesan (79) saw his team tame Madurai Panthers by 39 runs.
Debutant V. Hari Ragavendra’s fighting 98 (55b, 9x4, 6x6) kept Panthers in the hunt, but it proved insufficient as they suffered their first defeat.

briefs.headline: Golf | Important to perform well in multi-sport events: Gaganjeet Bhullar
briefs.bodyText:
Ace Indian golfer Gaganjeet Bhullar is a 11-time Asian Tour winner and an Arjuna Awardee.
But the 38-year-old, glowing with pride when recalling an accomplishment from two decades ago, believes that he is better known as an Asian Games silver medallist among the public.
Bhullar was a member of the India squad which made it to the podium in the men’s team event at the 2006 Doha Asiad. Speaking on the sidelines of an event hosted by Indian Golf Premier League (IGPL) franchise Vimtra Chennai Lions here on Friday, the veteran highlighted the importance of rising to the occasion in a multi-sport showpiece.
“Golf is an individual game, and we hardly get the opportunity to represent the country. So, when we get a chance at the Olympics or Asian Games, we should make our country proud. At the end of the day, we are Indians,” Bhullar said.
“I will give you an example. I was part of the silver medal-winning team in 2006. In some of the social gatherings, I am still remembered as an Asian Games silver medallist... it has been [nearly] 20 years. That is how important it is. It inspires the next generation... many youngsters; these are the people who need to play well.”
Bhullar sounded a warning to the Indian contingent that will travel to Aichi for the upcoming Asian Games in September-October but backed it to come good.
Yuvraj Sandhu, Veer Ahlawat and Saptak Talwar make up the men’s squad while the women’s team comprises Aditi Ashok, Diksha Dagar and Pranavi Urs.
“The women’s team is a strong contender. But overall, there is going to be stiff competition... it is going to be tough. South Korea is pretty strong, Japan is good and China has good youngsters. Competition makes you a better player, like it does in all big tournaments,” Bhullar added.

briefs.headline: Hockey World Cup: Guarded optimism as Indian men take on Wales in opener
briefs.deck: Hopefully, the jersey row will be pushed into the background as Harmanpreet & Co. attempt to end a 51-year medal drought in the event; the new format does not allow any scope for slip-ups
briefs.bodyText:
When the Indian men’s hockey team gets its World Cup campaign underway here on Saturday against Wales, casual viewers would be forgiven for mistaking it for co-host the Netherlands. The blue, which has been synonymous with Indian hockey, has been controversially painted over by saffron.
While Hockey India (HI) has sought to explain the logic behind the move, questions remain over who authorised it in the first place. The headlines in the lead-up to the World Cups were dominated by the boardroom decision and had little to do with the Indian men’s and women’s teams’ prospects.
Everyone involved will now hope there is something more substantial to talk about from Saturday. Although retaining the Asian Games gold medal seems like the more plausible target in the next two months, there is a real yearning for India to regain some of its past glory in the global showpiece. India’s only triumph came 51 years ago and in the 12 editions since, the best has been a fifth-place finish in 1982 and 1994.
Having fallen to No. 8 in the rankings, after a dismal Pro League campaign, India is a rank outsider in the mega event in the Netherlands and Belgium. Craig Fulton, who oversaw a collective improvement in the European leg of the Pro League, will hope his side doesn’t fall into familiar defensive lapses as it did in the first four months of the year. This Indian team has plenty of big-tournament experience to bank on. Captain Harmanpreet Singh, Manpreet Singh, Mandeep Singh and Amit Rohidas are veterans of several multi-nation tournaments. Yet, what might set apart Fulton’s men from the title contenders — Belgium, the Netherlands, England and Australia — is the depth in quality with proven match-winners across the pitch.
This will also be the first major tournament since P.R. Sreejesh’s retirement. The subsequent axing of Krishan Pathak, Sreejesh’s long-viewed successor earlier this year, has only added further scrutiny to India’s defensive woes. But after a shaky period, both Suraj Karkera and newcomer Mohith H.S., in particular, have impressed under the Indian goal.
India cannot afford any slip-ups in the new format. A strong start in the first round will be paramount for its ambitions of a deep run with the Netherlands and Argentina potentially awaiting in the next round.
On the Independence Day, the ‘new-look’ team will have the first opportunity to put behind questionable decision-making, both on and off the field, to show there is more at stake than the colour of the Indian jersey.
